title: I/O: Parquet, ORC, CSV, JSON, XML, text and Avro; Hadoop file systems; catalogs by configuration
verdict: data sources by `format`; `s3a://`, `abfss://`, `gs://` through Hadoop connectors; `spark.sql.catalog.*`
description: Spark reads and writes Parquet, ORC, CSV, JSON, XML, text and binary files with its built-in sources, and Avro with the bundled `spark-avro` module. Object stores go through Hadoop's file system connectors (`s3a://`, `abfss://`, `gs://`), which need their jars and credentials in the Hadoop configuration (`spark.hadoop.*`). Catalogs other than the session's are plugins named by `spark.sql.catalog.<name>` (Iceberg's `SparkCatalog`, Delta's `DeltaCatalog`, Unity Catalog's), each from its own package. Parquet keeps `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` and `TIMESTAMP_LTZ` apart and stores decimals by precision. Written and read back without a header or schema, a CSV column comes back as a `string` named `_c0`, and a JSON integer as a `bigint`; Parquet and ORC keep `int`.
reference: I/O is outside what a plan computes; sverify's `io` modules read and write the formats, and `sverify.spark_engine` hands Spark tables as temporary views.

evidence.note: `SELECT * FROM parquet.<dir>` reads back a table written `USING PARQUET`: `1`, an `int`
the same for CSV: `1` as `_c0`, a `string` (no header, no schema inference)
a JSON read from an `https://` path fails with `FAILED_READ_FILE.UNSUPPORTED_FILE_SYSTEM` from Hadoop's `HttpsFileSystem`: paths go through Hadoop file systems

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

evidence.note: the built-in sources registered by short name: CSV, JDBC, JSON, noop, ORC, Parquet, text, XML, binary files, and the streaming ones
Avro is registered by the separate `connector/avro` module
`lookupDataSource` finds a format by its short name through `ServiceLoader`, else by class name; a missing Avro raises `failedToFindAvroDataSourceError`
file paths are qualified through Hadoop's `Path.getFileSystem(hadoopConf)`
`Catalogs.load` reads the plugin class from `spark.sql.catalog.<name>` and instantiates it as a `CatalogPlugin`
